state:
Goal `core-regex-and-1-more`. `Core\Regex::compile`, `match`, `matchAll`, `matches` and `replace` owe
nothing but a perf row that is current, and `Core\Regex` has its class card. `replace` now reads its
replacement itself (`template` in `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/regex.rs`): a bare `$` takes at most two digits
as PHP's does, and `grow` asks the memory budget before the result grows. `replaceWith` builds its
result through `grow` too. `replaceWith`, `split` and `quote` still owe every proof, and their cards are
still in the old voice. The perf rows for all five landed members were recorded after the last edit to
`regex.rs`; the next edit to that file makes them stale again. `Core\Regex\Match` and
`Core\Regex\Pattern` are still listed in `CLASSES_STILL_OWING_A_CARD` in
`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/registry.rs`.

items.text: **`Core\Regex::replaceWith`** — owes about, examples, hostile, perf and a Rust test with `// covers: Core\Regex::replaceWith` (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`). Rewrite `REPLACE_WITH_DOC` in the plain voice the way `REPLACE_DOC` reads. Its callback is a real closure: the playbook's `closure_of` bullet is how a Rust test builds one. The attack can have the callback return a long text for every match, which `grow` must stop at the limit. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/regex.rs:358` `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/regex.rs:1969`

**`Core\Regex::split` and `Core\Regex::quote`** — the same proofs each; rewrite `SPLIT_DOC` and `QUOTE_DOC` the same way. `quote`'s attack feeds every special character and a very long text. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/regex.rs:398` `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/regex.rs:437` `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/regex.rs:2068` `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/regex.rs:2121`

**Record the rows** — `bun nv proofs --record-perf --group 'Core\Regex'` after the last edit to `regex.rs` (`--only 'Core\Regex'` is refused: that is a group, not a feature). `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/regex.rs:1969`

**`Core\Regex\Match`'s class card and proofs** — the `dossier-core-regex-match` check: a `ClassDoc` above the class's `CLASS` row, delete it from `CLASSES_STILL_OWING_A_CARD`, then `groups`, `offset` and `text` owe examples, hostile and perf. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/registry.rs:5283`

backlog: `Core\Regex::matches` allocates on every call — gap `nvs-stdlib/regex-matches-allocates-on-every-call` in `data/gaps/nvs-stdlib/`.
